Kamyanske (Former Dneprodzerzhynsk) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews first settled in Kamianske in the 1880s, alongside the development of the local steel industry; by 1897, the population reached 852, growing to 4,900 (3.8 percent) by 1939. The community survived pogroms in 1905 and during the Civil War; by 1931, 360 of 4,000 students at the local industrial school were Jewish, with 230 taught in Yiddish. Following the August 22, 1941 occupation, 206 Jews were murdered that same day, with several hundred more killed by month's end. The community revived after 1998, and in 2008 a replica of the Chabad-Lubavitch World Headquarters at 770 Eastern Parkway in Brooklyn — known as Beit Reuven or '770' — was built in the city. This cemetery, supposedly founded in the mid-20th century, was demolished around 1960 and is now a tram depot; per the local museum's director, some tombstones were reportedly moved to a nearby municipal cemetery, though none could actually be located there.
